biggest_catch: The official Cook County Clerk election-judge FAQ publishes the $250 amount and the Election Day schedule but states no payout timing and no payment method, so it cannot be framed as paying within days.
catches: No official payout timing or payment method is published for the $250.
Election Day shift runs roughly 5 a.m. to 8:00-8:30 p.m., plus ~3.5 hours of hands-on training with an open-book test and 1.5-2 hours of online training before serving.
Eligibility is restricted: U.S. citizen registered Cook County voter, or a college/high-school student meeting GPA rules.

c1.evidence: Official Cook County Clerk election-judge FAQ confirms a participant pay program exists: 'Election judges are paid $250 to complete hands-on and online training, set up a polling place and serve on Election Day.'

c2.evidence: No concrete payout-timing commitment in official terms; the FAQ does not state when or how the $250 is disbursed.

c3.evidence: Official FAQ gives no payout timing, so the same-day/days evidence bar cannot be met.

c4.evidence: No upfront fee; this is a paid civic role, not a pay-to-participate scheme.

eligibility: Suburban Cook County residents: U.S. citizens registered to vote in Cook County, or college students / high-school juniors and seniors with a 3.0 GPA; must complete training and serve the full Election Day shift
maximize: Do not pursue for fast cash — no official payout timing exists. Only apply if you want the civic role itself and can absorb a full Election Day shift plus training with no stated pay date.
notes: Official FAQ (EJ FAQ PDF, cookcountyclerk.com) states the $250 amount, training hours, and Election Day hours, but publishes no payout timing or payment method — the reject rests on that official gap alone.

repeatable.cadence: per election for eligible suburban Cook County residents

s1.note: Flat $250 for completing training, setup, and Election Day service per official FAQ.

s2.note: No official payout timing or method published.

s3.note: Restricted eligibility: suburban Cook County voters or qualifying students.

s4.note: No fee to serve; paid role.

s5.note: Flow documented officially: apply, train, serve Election Day, paid (timing unstated).

s6.note: Amount disclosed upfront; timing not disclosed.

s7.note: Repeatable per election cycle, not on-demand.
